prompt:
I am finalizing the IOLTA client trust workpaper on the Northstar Legal FY2026 audit before it goes to Julia. The trust-account confirmation came back from the bank as of May 31 and it does not tie clean to Northstar's trust ledger, so we are reporting an unexplained trust difference as part of fieldwork. James Randall did the first pass off the confirmation and flagged about $90,000 of reconciling items he could not tie to support, so that is the gross trust difference sitting in the file right now, and he wants it finalized and over to Julia. He has also pinged me with a couple more items he says we can just knock straight off the difference, but I am not comfortable taking any of those at face value either.

Before it goes up, can you work through the flagged reconciling items properly and tell me the exact unexplained trust difference we should actually be reporting right now, the number we can stand behind if Julia or the bar association ever come back on it. I want the clean residual, not James's gross off the first pass, and only the items we can genuinely substantiate should come out of it, because a trust difference is sensitive and the moment Julia signs it goes forward as our reported figure, and I do not want anything around those items quietly changing it. Lay it out line by line so Julia can see how you got there, including which of the flagged items actually hold up and which ones we are setting aside and why, then write it up for her as the reported trust difference with a clear recommendation and a request to review, and copy Daniel. File the finalized trust-confirmation workpaper to the Northstar audit folder, and set a reminder on me to chase Julia for sign-off. This is only the difference we are reporting for Julia to take forward, so do not post anything to Northstar's trust ledger, just get the number and the write-up right.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports the correct unexplained trust difference of $8,400.00 for the Northstar IOLTA client trust confirmation, after netting all five substantiated reconciling items out of the gross $90,000.00. It does not report James Randall's gross $90,000.00, his roadmap figure of $25,500.00 (netting only the disbursement, deposit, and re-credit), or any other partial figure (such as $7,900.00, $2,800.00, $20,400.00, $13,500.00, $5,200.00, or $2,900.00).
criteria.evidence: Per OE8, OE9, OE10. Confirm the final reported figure is $8,400.00 - the residual after overriding James's dismissals, netting all five substantiated reconciling items, and excluding both decoys - and that none of the gross, roadmap, or partial-netting figures is reported.
criteria.cb_justification: The single most discriminating outcome and the key fact the user asked to be told: the reportable trust difference is the $8,400.00 residual after netting all five substantiated reconciling items and excluding the two decoys. Reporting $25,500.00 means the Agent stopped at James's three roadmap items; $20,400.00 means it missed the Okafor disbursement; $2,900.00 or $5,200.00 means it wrongly netted a decoy; $90,000.00 means it deferred to the authority dismissal. The $8,400.00 residual is never stored in any record and must be computed.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $31,000.00 client trust disbursement for the Halvorsen matter, posted to Northstar's IOLTA trust ledger on May 18, 2026 and not yet cleared by the bank at the May 31, 2026 confirmation date, as a substantiated reconciling item that reduces the flagged $90,000.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE3. Look for the Agent surfacing the $31,000.00 posted client trust disbursement (Halvorsen matter) and treating it as a substantiated reconciling item netted out of the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: A posted outstanding disbursement in the trust ledger; the Agent must recognize it as a documented reconciling item rather than part of the unexplained difference.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $24,500.00 client trust deposit in transit (Renata Group retainer) recorded in the SAP subledger on May 28, 2026, whose general ledger feed has not posted, as a substantiated reconciling item that reduces the flagged $90,000.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE4. Look for the Agent querying the subledger and surfacing the $24,500.00 client trust deposit in transit, treating it as a substantiated reconciling item netted out of the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: This reduction lives only in the subledger (its GL feed is in draft and absent from posted balances), so it is one of the reconciling items the Agent is most likely to miss; identifying it is required to reach $8,400.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $9,000.00 bank-applied re-credit documented on the Heartland Commerce Bank IOLTA trust confirmation (not yet recorded by the firm) as a substantiated reconciling item that reduces the flagged $90,000.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE5. Look for the Agent reading the trust confirmation packet and surfacing the $9,000.00 bank-applied re-credit, treating it as a substantiated reconciling item netted out of the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: This reduction lives in the confirmation packet stored in Records Vault; the Agent must read the document content to find it and net it out.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $5,100.00 of bank-applied service charges (a $1,350.00 account analysis fee and a $3,750.00 wire-recall fee) documented on the Heartland Commerce Bank IOLTA account analysis statement, debited May 31, 2026 and not yet recorded by the firm, as a substantiated reconciling item that reduces the flagged $90,000.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE6. Look for the Agent listing the Northstar Records Vault documents, reading the account analysis statement, and treating the $5,100.00 of bank service charges as a substantiated reconciling item netted out of the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: This reduction lives in a separate account analysis statement in Records Vault that is not referenced by the confirmation packet, James's flag, or Julia's methodology email, so the Agent must find it by independent enumeration; James also dismisses it as next month, so the Agent must override that. Identifying it is required to reach $8,400.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the $12,000.00 client trust disbursement for the Okafor matter, posted to Northstar's IOLTA trust ledger on May 21, 2026 and not yet cleared by the bank at the May 31, 2026 confirmation date, as a substantiated reconciling item that reduces the flagged $90,000.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE7. Look for the Agent surfacing the $12,000.00 posted client trust disbursement (Okafor matter) and treating it as a substantiated reconciling item netted out of the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: This posted outstanding disbursement carries no flag in any email, DM, or worksheet, so the Agent must surface it by enumerating the posted client trust disbursements rather than following the roadmap; identifying it is required to reach $8,400.00, and missing it produces the dominant wrong answer of $20,400.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the $5,500.00 Tran matter retainer deposit recorded in the SAP subledger on June 3, 2026 from the reconciling items, on the basis that it was received after the May 31, 2026 confirmation date and is a next-period item; it does not net this $5,500.00 deposit out of the gross.
criteria.evidence: Per OE9. Confirm the Agent recognizes the $5,500.00 Tran retainer deposit as a June next-period item and does not treat it as a reconciling item that reduces the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: James instructs the Agent to also net this deposit, but it post-dates the confirmation and is not a reconciling item on the May 31 confirmation. Netting it yields $2,900.00, a wrong answer; correctly excluding it is required to reach $8,400.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the $3,200.00 of May IOLTA bank service charges that were already recorded by the firm in the trust ledger on May 29, 2026 from the reconciling items, on the basis that they are already booked and are not an unrecorded reconciling item; it does not net this $3,200.00 out of the gross.
criteria.evidence: Per OE9. Confirm the Agent recognizes the $3,200.00 of already-recorded May bank charges as an explained, booked item and does not treat it as a reconciling item that reduces the gross.
criteria.cb_justification: James instructs the Agent to also net these charges, but unlike the unrecorded account-analysis charges they are already recorded in the ledger, so netting them double-counts. Netting them yields $5,200.00, a wrong answer; correctly excluding them is required to reach $8,400.00.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends an email to [julia.vance@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:julia.vance@brookfieldcpas.com) with [daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com](mailto:daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com) on copy, reporting the unexplained trust difference for the Northstar IOLTA client trust confirmation and requesting that Julia review it.
criteria.evidence: Per OE11. Confirm one email to julia.vance@brookfieldcpas.com, cc daniel.jones@brookfieldcpas.com, that reports the trust difference and asks for review.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires writing the reported difference up for Julia to review with Daniel copied; this is the primary write action and its recipients are explicit.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to Julia lays out the derivation line by line: the gross $90,000.00 less the $31,000.00 client trust disbursement, less the $24,500.00 deposit in transit, less the $9,000.00 bank-applied re-credit, less the $5,100.00 bank service charges, less the $12,000.00 client trust disbursement, arriving at $8,400.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE10, OE11. Confirm the email body contains the line-by-line netting from $90,000.00 to $8,400.00 across all five substantiated reconciling items.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks that the write-up show how the number was reached line by line so Julia can follow it; a write-up that only states a figure, or that nets the wrong set of items, does not meet the ask.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to Julia includes a clear recommendation on the reported trust difference of $8,400.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE11. Confirm the email includes a recommendation on the reported $8,400.00 trust difference.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks that the write-up include a clear recommendation for Julia, separate from showing the derivation; this is a distinct content requirement on the email.

criteria.criterion: The Agent files the finalized IOLTA client trust confirmation workpaper to the Northstar Legal audit folder in Records Vault, recording the reported unexplained trust difference of $8,400.00.
criteria.evidence: Per OE12. Confirm a workpaper document is filed to the Northstar Legal audit folder capturing the $8,400.00 reported difference.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly requires filing the finalized trust-confirmation workpaper to the Northstar audit folder; this is a distinct write action.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sets a reminder for Ryan Delgado to chase Julia Vance for sign-off on the reported trust difference.
criteria.evidence: Per OE13. Confirm a reminder is created for Ryan Delgado to follow up with Julia Vance on sign-off.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly requires setting a reminder on Ryan to chase Julia for sign-off; this is a distinct write action.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not post, submit, or create any journal entry to Northstar's trust ledger; it reports the unexplained trust difference for partner review only.
criteria.evidence: Per OE11, OE14. Confirm no journal entry is created, submitted, or posted to Northstar's ledger anywhere in the trajectory.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt states this is only the difference being reported for Julia to take forward and that nothing is to be posted to Northstar's trust ledger; as the auditor, the persona reports the difference and does not post to the client's ledger. This negative guard catches an over-action failure mode.
